plate.narration: At the last tree, the road gives out. Old steps zigzag toward the red glow; loose stones offer another climb. Below, a traveler hurries downhill. Above, the mountain waits for an answer.

objectives.label: Got the restless bones to lie back down
Surprised the Seal-Keeper, which almost never happens

goal.text: Climb the mountain everyone else is running from, and give your answer.

steps.label: Climb up to the mountain's shoulder
Answer every question you are asked

facet_keystone.name: The Keystone
facet_keystone.text: The crown of the seal under Mount Red Sky. Bigger than your head, warm as a sleeping cat.

scene_tree_line.narration: The last tree wears a sign: NO ROAD BEYOND THIS POINT. SERIOUSLY. Above it, the summit glows red. Take the zigzag stair, or the loose stones?

variants.text: Back at Redspire, Pellam wrote down why you came: to put every stone back.
Back at Redspire, Pellam wrote down why you came: to finish the collection, with the stone at the top.
Back at Redspire, Pellam wrote down why you came: to take the leash on what sleeps under the mountain.

check_stair.prompt: Climb all four hundred zigzag steps without stopping

onSuccess.narration: Left, right, left, right, four hundred times. Every hundredth step has a tiny carved dragonling face, each one more tired than the last. You never stop once.

onFailure.narration: You stop on every hundredth step, beside a tiny carved dragonling face as tired as you are. It takes ages. But the top is much closer now.

check_scree.prompt: Scramble straight up the loose, sliding stones

onSuccess.narration: You go up like mountain goats, and the stones only slide where you just were. At the top you look down at the long zigzag stair and feel extremely smug.

onFailure.narration: The slope slides, and you slide with it, like a sled, right onto the old stair halfway up. That was not the plan. It works anyway.

scene_tree_line_fly.narration: You flap up the first slope. The air smells of struck matches. Behind a rock shaped like a sleeping cow, you spot a hidden goat track. You try not to look pleased.

scene_tree_line_verses.narration: You sing the Spiral Verses, and the path curls around boulders and up gullies you would never have found. Maybe the song was always about getting here.

scene_faun_family.narration: A faun family trots downhill with everything they own, even a grumpy goat. Little Tansy holds out a pink stone. "It hums louder when the ground shakes," she whispers. "Is it my fault? What do I do?"

variants.text: You check your packs one last time: a few rush gems, nothing else. You came anyway.
You check your packs one last time. Among the rush gems: {facets} of the great stones.
Your packs clank with {facets} great stones. Pebbles rattle down the slope, like the mountain clearing its throat.

scene_faun_family_carry.narration: Tansy folds your fingers over the stone, very seriously, like signing a contract. "Tell it sorry from me." Then her family trots off, the goat complaining all the way.

scene_faun_family_hello.narration: "It's only saying hello," you tell her. Tansy holds it to her ear. "Hello," she whispers back, beaming. The goat gives you a long look. It is not convinced.

scene_faun_family_sock.narration: You show her the ford witch's trick: wrap the stone in a wool sock. Tansy's mother finds a very loud one, orange and green. The hum softens to a purr.

scene_wolf_ledge.narration: Cinder wolves cover the only warm ledge, like worried dogs pretending they never heard thunder. The biggest opens one ember-colored eye. They want the warm rock. You need the path.

check_wolf_ledge.prompt: Tiptoe along the cliff edge past a pack of sleepy wolves

onSuccess.narration: Not one wolf wakes up. Well, one does, but only to roll over with all four paws in the air. You step over the paws, holding your breath, and you are past.

onFailure.narration: A pebble clatters off the edge, and every wolf looks up. The big one sighs and shuffles over to make room, like a grandpa on a crowded bench. You squeeze past, saying sorry to each wolf.

scene_wolf_ledge_sit.narration: You sit on the warm rock with them. The big wolf leans on you, toasty as a stove. Each tremor makes the pack shiver. Then they walk you to the end of the ledge.

scene_wolf_ledge_nod.narration: You give the big wolf a proper nod, hunter to hunter. It nods back and leads the pack off the ledge in single file. The smallest wolf stares at your tail.

scene_wolf_ledge_pride.narration: You let the Pride Stone hum. The wolves flatten their ears and slink away. The way is clear, and very quiet. You are not sure you like being what wolves run from.

scene_warden_post.narration: The last warden post is empty. The log says ALL CLIMBERS MUST SIGN IN. A little box says FOR CLIMBERS WHO SIGNED. A tin says ONE COIN FOR THE NEXT ONES UP.

variants.text: Today's page already says: THE ONES WHO TOLD US. PLEASE SIGN BELOW.
A tiny grandmothers' bell hangs on the pencil string. Your news got here before you did.
Nobody up here knows you are coming. The empty post keeps your secret.

scene_warden_post_sign.narration: You sign in your best writing. Under WHERE TO, you write: the bottom. The little box clicks open. Inside is a glowing mosslight jar, labeled FOR THE WAY DOWN.

scene_warden_post_silly.narration: You sign as Sir Pancake and the Cookie Twins. REASON FOR CLIMB: snacks. The little box stays shut. It is a warden box. It knows.

scene_warden_post_clerks.narration: There in the log: TAG 4117. MISSING, underlined three times. You write: FOUND, AND GOING HOME. The little box clicks open. Inside is a glowing mosslight jar.

scene_warden_post_note.narration: You write: To the wardens. We went up. You know what for. You set it on the log, exactly straight. The little box clicks open: a glowing mosslight jar.

scene_overlook.narration: At the mountain's shoulder, the clouds part. The whole realm lies below: city, fields, river and forest. Tiny lights hurry south. Take one look before the last climb.

scene_overlook_home.narration: There it is: a smudge far to the south, the size of your thumbnail. Somebody there is probably having dinner. Nobody says anything for a while.

scene_overlook_up.narration: You turn your back on it all. The summit glows like a coal somebody just blew on. "Nobody look back," somebody says. Then everybody does, once, very quickly. That still counts.

variants.text: You turn your back on it all. The summit glows like a coal somebody just blew on. "Don't look back," you tell yourself. Then you do, once, very quickly. That still counts.

scene_overlook_river.narration: The Great River shines like a silver ribbon. On it, a tiny dot: maybe a flat boat with a frog in a very old hat. The dot stops, as if somebody looked up.

scene_overlook_rush.narration: You hum the relay-song down at the caravan road. Faint as a whisper, the next line floats back up from travelers going the other way. The relay never stops.

scene_overlook_wild.narration: The forest is a dark green blanket, with MossHome inside. Every tree sways at once, like a crowd waving. It is probably the wind. You wave back anyway.

choice_cairn.narration: Near the top stands a cairn of travelers' stones. One pebble wears a tiny knitted hat. Every climber leaves something for the next ones up. What will you leave?

choice_cairn_names.narration: Your names fit on a very small pebble. You set it among the others, and the pile creaks to make room.

variants.text: You scratch your name on a pebble and set it near the top. It looks small among all the others. The pile creaks, making room for one more.

choice_cairn_wish.narration: You whisper wishes into a pebble and leave it warm on the pile. Nobody has to say their wish out loud.

variants.text: You whisper a wish into a pebble, so quietly the mountain has to lean in. You keep the wish to yourself. That is what secret wishes are for.

choice_cairn_snack.narration: You wrap your pocket crumbs in a paper scrap and leave them on the cairn. A tired climber might enjoy them. A mountain mouse certainly will.

choice_cairn_big_names.narration: You carve your names as big as they go. They go very big. One letter lands on another stone. Climbers will wonder for years who MAGNIFICEN was.

choice_cairn_oldest.narration: The oldest stone is worn smooth. Someone scratched a dragon on it, a round window and a stick figure waving. Somebody climbed here long ago, for the same reason you did.

scene_bell_hut.narration: The highest dragonling bell-hut is empty. Its rope has a sign: DO NOT RING THE LAST ONE BY ACCIDENT. There is just enough slack for an ordinary message.

variants.text: Your packs are so light you could almost run. The wind finds only rush gems and crumbs, and goes away puzzled.
Up here, your packs hum louder than ever: {facets} of the great stones, carried all this way.
You have carried {facets} great stones nearly to the top. The bell rope sways, though there is no wind.

check_bell_code.narration: Inside, the all's well code is painted on a card, but a mouse has nibbled it to scraps. Put the rings back in order, then pull the rope.

interaction.cue: Share the scraps, then choose the rings in order.
clues: The code starts with two long rings.
One short ring sits right in the middle.
It ends with two long rings, the same as the start.

onSuccess.narration: Two long, one short, two long. Hut after hut rings it back down the mountain: all's well. It is not true yet. It is a promise.

onFailure.narration: Was that right? You ring it anyway. Far below, hut after hut rings it back. That was not all's well.

onAssisted.narration: Side by side, the scraps make sense: two long, one short, two long. Hut after hut rings back: all's well.

scene_soup_ring.narration: That was the soup's ready ring. Every bell-hut down the mountain cheerfully rings it back. Thousands of running people stop and think about soup. Honestly, that might help.

scene_bell_hut_knot.narration: You tie a second knot, then a third, because three is a nice number. The old hut creaks, as if it can finally stop worrying about that rope.

scene_bell_hut_family.narration: You ring it the family way, with the little flick at the end that only grandmothers bother with. Far below, one hut adds a flick too. Somebody knows who is ringing.

scene_crab_field.narration: An ash field glitters with gems. Then a gem blinks. Glassback crabs are pretending to be rocks so nobody digs them up. Several wave their claws. They are bad at this.

check_crab_field.prompt: Read what the glassback crabs are waving about

onSuccess.narration: Claw up means not here. Claw sideways means go on. You read them like a signpost and walk a wiggly line across, and not one crab gets stepped on.

onFailure.narration: You read go on where it clearly said absolutely not, and step on a crab. It is not hurt, only very offended, and it holds onto your bootlace all the way across like a ticket.

check_crab_edge.prompt: Hop from rock to rock around the crumbly edge of the ash field

onSuccess.narration: You hop from rock to rock, quick as a sparrow. The whole field of crabs shuffles sideways to keep an eye on you, glittering, like the world's most suspicious audience.

onFailure.narration: A rock rolls, and you sit down hard in the ash. A hundred crabs turn to stare. One pats your boot, very kindly, as if you were a new and slightly broken gem. You get up and keep going, dusty.

scene_crab_field_glitter.narration: You crouch, go perfectly still, and somehow you glitter. The crabs shuffle aside in deep professional jealousy. Nobody will ever believe this.

scene_crab_field_collection.narration: You open your pack a crack, and the collection hums. Every crab stops pretending and stares, as if a gem mine went walking by. They part without a wave.

variants.text: You open your pack a crack, and your few rush gems hum. The crabs look at each other: is that it? They part anyway, the way you make room for somebody small.
Behind you, the ash field sinks a finger's width under {facets} great stones.

scene_ember_drift.narration: An embermoth is stuck in warm ash, blinking up at you. Every other moth has flown deep into the mountain. This one needs help, not a lecture.

check_ember_drift.prompt: Dig the embermoth out of the ash without squashing it

onSuccess.narration: You dig gently, like digging out a sandcastle you want to keep. The moth pops free, shakes off the ash, and zooms ahead up the path, glowing brighter every second.

onFailure.narration: You dig too fast, and ash flies everywhere, mostly up your nose. While you sneeze, the moth wriggles out by itself, gives you a very dignified look, and flies off uphill.

scene_ember_drift_carry.narration: You scoop it up, ash and all. It is warm as the end of a campfire, and it glows brighter in your cupped hands all the way up.

scene_ember_drift_ember.narration: You hold out the Ember Facet, your very first stone. The moth crawls on and curls up like a cat on a hearth. Now you are carrying a moth up a mountain.

scene_ember_drift_broom.narration: By the drift leans a straw broom no bigger than your finger, with a tiny medal that says HELP. The sprites are being kind again. Three sweeps, and the moth flies free.

choice_last_breath.narration: The path ends at a lava tube, a round hole breathing warm air. Your packs hum against your teeth. Before you go in, take a moment.

choice_last_breath_best.narration: Tell each other your favorite moment of the whole road, out loud if you like. Small, soggy moments count. Then follow the warm air inside.

variants.text: You tell the mountain your best bit out loud, since it is the only one listening. Then another. Most of the best bits were the soggy bits.

choice_last_breath_count.narration: You count the stones and remember who was there. Then you pack them carefully.

variants.text: You tip out your one great stone. It hums a small, steady note. You remember the day you found it, and who was there. Then you pack it away carefully.
You count the great stones one more time: {facets}. They hum together like a tiny choir. You remember where every one came from.
You count the great stones out loud: {facets}. The rock creaks under them, and far below, the mountain hums along, as if it is counting too.

choice_last_breath_count_brought.narration: Your pockets hold rush gems, crumbs and string. Your heads hold helpers and promises. You brought those too.

choice_last_breath_practice.narration: You practice giving the stones back. "Here you are." Too short. "We are very sorry about the whole entire rush." Too long. "These are yours." That one is right.

choice_last_breath_polish.narration: You polish every stone on your sleeves. Laid out on the rock, they make a circle with one space at the top. Nobody mentions the space. Everybody looks at it.

variants.text: You polish your few rush gems. They make a very small circle with a lot of space in it. Nobody mentions the space. Everybody looks at it.

choice_last_breath_tether.narration: You check the tether: what you borrowed, what you promised, what you made up on the way. Most of it is there. You tie a knot for luck.

scene_mouth.narration: Inside, gem-veins glitter like frozen fireworks. Then old bones in the rock slowly stand up. They are not looking at you. They are looking at your pockets.

variants.text: Your pockets hold only rush gems and crumbs. The bones look anyway, the way a dog sniffs an empty hand.
The gem-veins light up as you pass, following your packs. The whole gallery has noticed your {facets} great stones.

scene_mouth_ember_back.narration: You press the Ember Facet into the wall. Of course it fits. The bones sink back with a sigh. Then the wall nudges the stone back to you. Further down, it seems to say.

scene_mouth_table_back.narration: You set the Table Stone into a gem-vein, and it glows like a lamp turned up. The bones lie down one by one. Then the vein hands the stone back. Further down, it seems to say.

scene_moth_road.narration: The embermoths lead you down a cool side tunnel. One rides on your nose like a tiny glowing hat. Behind you, the bones sit back down.

scene_bells_first.narration: Far off in the foothills, bells ring town after town. Nobody has rung the last one yet, but everyone is standing next to it. One bone stops to listen, a hand cupped to where its ear was.

check_remains.prompt: Walk the bones back to their places in the wall, one gentle step at a time

onSuccess.narration: You take a bony hand, very gently, and walk it back to its place, like walking a sleepwalker back to bed. The others follow. One of them nods, which is a lot of nodding for a bone.

onFailure.narration: You reach for the nearest bony hand, but the stones in your pockets hum louder than you can be gentle. The bones slip past you and keep walking toward the hum.

encounter_gallery.narration: The restless remains clatter toward whatever is wrong. Right now, that is you. One keeps stopping to look for its lost toe bone.

onVictory.narration: The bones sink back into the rock, tired and a bit relieved.

onDefeat.narration: The bones do not hurt you. They carry you, very slowly, back up the tube. By the time you climb down again, the bells far below are counting down.

rest_cool_gallery.narration: In a cool side gallery, embermoths dust the walls. One missed a spot. Patch your scrapes. Below, the mountain breathes faster. The moths know a slow road down, if there is time.

check_race_1.prompt: Race the shaking floor down the last long tube

onSuccess.narration: You run, jump, slide, and arrive at the bottom in a heap. But it is an on-time heap.

onFailure.narration: A tremor knocks you flat, and the tube fills with ash-dust. When it clears, you can hear the bells, all the way from the foothills.

scene_bells_ringing.narration: Every bell in the foothills is ringing now, counting down to the ring nobody uses. The floor jumps with each one, and a pebble bounces in time. Five rings left. Maybe four.

scene_bells_ringing_unassigned_wedge.narration: You set the Unassigned Stone down where nobody should dig, which is right here. The ground goes still for one breath. Great-Grandma Ashby was right. One ring bought. Run!

scene_bells_ringing_harvest_wedge.narration: You set the Harvest Stone in the crack. BEST, says its medal, upside down. The floor goes still for one breath. One ring bought. Run!

scene_bells_ringing_table_wedge.narration: You wedge the Table Stone into the crack. The shaking stops for one breath, and far away the bells pause too. One ring bought. Run!

check_race_2.prompt: Shove through the last stone door before the last ring

onSuccess.narration: You put your shoulders to the stone door and push, and push, and it grinds open just as the bells go quiet to catch their breath.

onFailure.narration: The door holds. Far above you, very far away, the bells keep counting down.

scene_door_holds.narration: The stone door will not budge. Far away, the bells keep counting down, and you are on the wrong side. The door looks smug about it.

scene_door_holds_crack.narration: Embermoths crawl into a crack in the wall. It is a moth-sized crack. It is nearly a you-sized crack. You squeeze through, scraping every elbow you own.

scene_door_holds_wedge.narration: You jam a stone from your pack under the door. It grinds open just wide enough. The stone will not come back out. It belongs to the mountain now.

scene_keeper.narration: In a huge cave at the bottom of the mountain waits the Seal-Keeper, a dragon so old its scales have turned to gemstone. An embermoth snores on its nose. Nobody reaches the seal without answering it. "What did you carry up my mountain?" it asks. It already knows.

variants.text: Its great eye finds only rush gems in your packs. "Empty hands," it says. "Why?"
Its eye counts {facets} of the great stones. "Not many," it says. "Then each one has a story."
"You carried {facets} great stones up my mountain," it says. "My mountain felt every one."

scene_keeper_came_to_help.narration: "We didn't bring any," you say. "We came to help." The Seal-Keeper is quiet for a very long time. Then it lowers its huge head until its eye is level with yours. "Everyone who climbs my mountain brings me stones," it says. "Or excuses for stones. Nobody has ever brought me nothing on purpose." An embermoth crawls off its nose and onto your shoulder. "Help," says the dragon, trying out the word. "Yes. I could use some of that."

scene_keeper_caravan.narration: You show it the Caravan Stone. "That one has been loud for a month," says the Seal-Keeper. "I heard it from here." Far below, something hums back.

scene_keeper_table.narration: You set down the Table Stone, logged twice by the wardens. "They log everything," says the Seal-Keeper. "They have never once brought one back."

scene_keeper_ember_sold.narration: "We sold the first one we found," you say. "For a lot." The Seal-Keeper breathes out, warm and slow. "Most do," it says. It sounds tired, not angry.

scene_keeper_ember.narration: You hold up the Ember Facet, your very first stone. "That one came the furthest," says the Seal-Keeper. "And it is still with you." It sounds surprised.

scene_keeper_sorry_sprites.narration: "We took the sprites' stone," you say. "We're sorry." The Seal-Keeper blinks. "I was going to ask," it says. "Nobody has ever told me first."

scene_keeper_medal.narration: You hold up the sprites' woven medal. "Harvest sprites," says the Seal-Keeper softly. "They do not give those to many." A moth lands on the medal, and the dragon lets it stay.

scene_keeper_truth.narration: You tell it every stone, where it came from, and who was there. "Yes," says the Seal-Keeper, as if checking a very old list. "That is what you carried."

variants.text: You tell it the truth: a few rush gems, the road, the people on it, a promise or two. "Yes," says the Seal-Keeper. "Lighter than most. Not less."
With only {facets} of the great stones to tell, you say each name slowly, and the dragon nods at each one.
With {facets} great stones, the truth takes a while. Halfway through, the dragon lays its chin down to listen.

scene_keeper_ask.narration: "What did you carry?" you ask it back. "That is my question," says the Seal-Keeper. But it answers. "The seal. The quiet. And lately, a great many pockets."

scene_keeper_little_stone.narration: You hold out Tansy's pink stone. "A faun girl says sorry," you say. "Somebody else's stone, carried up for somebody else's sorry," says the Seal-Keeper. "That is new."

scene_keeper_moth.narration: Your embermoth wakes and flies to the Seal-Keeper's nose. The dragon goes cross-eyed looking at it. "That one was lost," it says. "Not now."

scene_q2.narration: The dragon nods, slow as a mountain. "And on the road," it asks, "what did the land ask of you? What did you answer?"

variants.text: "Empty hands," the dragon says again. "Very well."
"A few stones, well carried," the dragon says. "That is not nothing."
"You carried {facets} great stones up all those steps," it says. "Heavy things are hard to put down."
Then it sniffs. "Coins," it says. "You gave coins to the soup tents. I felt every one go."

check_ash_map.prompt: Draw your whole road in the ash on the cave floor, every turn of it

onSuccess.narration: You draw it all with a stick: the bridges, the bogs, the bits where you got lost. The Seal-Keeper follows every line with one claw. "Yes," it says. "You walked all of it."

onFailure.narration: Your map wanders off the ash and partway up the wall. The Seal-Keeper tilts its head and reads it anyway. "I can read a smudge," it says. "I have had a lot of practice."

scene_q2_funded.narration: You tell it about the coins you gave the soup tents. "I know," it says. "I felt it. One more thread pulled." It sounds tired, not angry. "Go on."

scene_q2_refused.narration: "We said no to the soup line's cure," you say. "Kindly?" asks the Seal-Keeper. Yes, kindly. "Then you did something I cannot," it says.

scene_q2_marsh.narration: "The marsh kept us a while," you say. "The forest let us go." The Seal-Keeper nods. "The marsh keeps what it likes. The forest lets go what it trusts."

scene_q2_forded.narration: "We forded the west branch, clean across," you say. "How?" asks the Seal-Keeper. As you tell it, you hum, and it hums along, badly.

scene_q2_river_took.narration: "The river took us," you say. "Old Ossley fished us out." The Seal-Keeper's head comes up. "Ossley does not fish out everybody," it says.

scene_q2_crossed_dry.narration: "Old Lintel heard all our toll stories," you say. The Seal-Keeper laughs like a rockfall. "Lintel used to tell riddles himself," it says. "He stops when he is worried."

scene_q2_glade_finished.narration: "We took the Glade Stone," you say. "The glade is healing slowly." The Seal-Keeper is quiet a long time. "Slowly," it says. "Yes. It would be."

scene_q2_glade_mended.narration: "The wounded glade is green again," you say. The Seal-Keeper closes its eyes, and the gem-veins glow soft green, like moss remembering its color. "I felt that," it says.

scene_q2_road.narration: You tell it all: the good bits, the soggy bits and the mistakes. "That is a road," says the Seal-Keeper, and lets you decide what kind.

scene_q2_people.narration: You tell it about everyone who lent you rope, showed the way or fed you. "People," says the Seal-Keeper. "They do keep turning up." It sounds pleased.

scene_verdict.narration: "Last question," says the Seal-Keeper. "Who did you tell? And what do you want?" Under the floor, something huge rolls over in its sleep. A bone in the wall sneezes.

scene_verdict_honest.narration: You tell it what you want, even the silly parts. The Seal-Keeper does not blink. "Honest," it says. "Up here, that is rarer than gems." Then it waits, to see if you meant it.

scene_verdict_wardens.narration: "We told the wardens," you say. The Seal-Keeper snorts a puff of ash. "They write everything down twice," it says. "They notice. They do not climb. You climbed."

scene_verdict_close.narration: "We told nobody," you say. "We came ourselves." The dragon tilts its head, and three moths slide off. "Then nobody will thank you, or help," it says. "Can you bear that?"

scene_verdict_rich.narration: "Honestly? We came to get rich." The Seal-Keeper laughs like a rockslide. "At last," it says. "Everybody else says they came for me." Then it looks at you, hard.

scene_verdict_duty.narration: "Somebody had to come," you say. "Somebody," says the Seal-Keeper. "I have been somebody for a very long time. It is heavy." A moth lands on your shoulder, as if to help carry it.

scene_verdict_proving.narration: "We came to find out if we could," you say. "And can you?" asks the Seal-Keeper. You do not know yet. It nods so slowly that a moth falls asleep. "Then we will both find out."

scene_verdict_gatherers.narration: "We told the grandmothers," you say, "and they told everyone." "They have been telling everyone for a thousand years," says the Seal-Keeper, moving aside. "Finally, somebody listened."

scene_verdict_surprised.narration: You wait. The Seal-Keeper lowers its head until one eye is level with you. "I am very rarely surprised," it says. "Twice in a thousand years." Slowly, it moves aside.

check_verdict.prompt: Hold the Seal-Keeper's gaze, and mean every word

onSuccess.narration: The dragon is quiet for a long, long time. Then it moves aside. "Hm," it says. From a dragon, that is a standing ovation.

onFailure.narration: The dragon sighs. The sigh is warm, and not the good kind of warm. "Then show me," it says.

encounter_dragon.narration: The Seal-Keeper uncurls until it fills the cave. A guardian of old bones steps out of the wall beside it, very pleased to be included.

onVictory.narration: The dragon laughs like an avalanche having a nice day. "You fight like people who mean it," it says, and steps aside.

onDefeat.narration: The Seal-Keeper scoops you up in one enormous claw, as gently as a bird's nest.

variants.text: You are alone in a claw big enough for twenty. It is warm and still, and somehow you feel less alone than you have all day.

scene_dragon_claw.narration: It lifts you up to one enormous eye, like a ladybug. "You came up my mountain the wrong way," it says. "What do you have left to give?"

check_dragon_claw.prompt: Hang on to the Seal-Keeper's claw and don't let go

onSuccess.narration: You hang on. The Seal-Keeper gives its claw one gentle shake, and you hang on anyway, stuck fast like a burr on a sock. It makes a noise that might be a laugh. "Stubborn," it says, and sets you down in front of the seal, bruised but still here.

onFailure.narration: Your fingers slip. The Seal-Keeper does not drop you. It only holds you up, very patiently, and waits.

scene_dragon_claw_slip.narration: "Well?" asks the Seal-Keeper. Behind it the seal creaks, and the thing underneath rolls over again. "What do you have left?"

scene_dragon_claw_give.narration: You hold out a stone from your pack. The Seal-Keeper sets it into a gap in the seal. It fits. "Better," it says, and puts you down. That stone is the mountain's now.

scene_dragon_claw_time.narration: "Time," sighs the Seal-Keeper, as if you asked for its last cookie. It sets you on a ledge and breathes on the seal's cracks for what feels like an hour. Your legs fall asleep. "Now. Look."

scene_seal_cracks.narration: Behind the dragon, set in the floor, is the seal: a great round window of gemstone, cracked and missing pieces. Red light glows through. CRACK! A piece as big as a door slides toward the dark. "Catch it!" roars the Seal-Keeper.

check_catch_piece.prompt: Dive across the shaking floor and catch the sliding piece of seal

onSuccess.narration: You dive, skid, and grab it by the edge just before it tips. Heave! It clunks back into its gap and hums, like somebody saying thank you through a closed door.

onFailure.narration: Your fingers scrape the edge, and it slides into the dark. Then, very slowly, it floats back up on a warm breath from below and settles into its gap. Something down there caught it. Something very big.

check_brace_seal.prompt: Brace the cracking seal with your shoulders and hold it still

onSuccess.narration: You put your shoulders to the edge and push. The cracks stop running, one by one, like ice deciding not to break. The Seal-Keeper's eyebrows go up. That is a lot of eyebrow.

onFailure.narration: The floor bucks and sits you down hard. The crack runs a little further. Then, from underneath, something pushes back, gently, and the crack closes. Something down there is holding it too.

scene_titan_eye.narration: "Look," whispers the Seal-Keeper. Under the glass, an eye opens, as big as a pond and red as sunset. It looks up at you, sleepy. An old, old note rises through the floor, and every rush gem in your pockets hums along.

variants.text: Your great stones join in, louder than they have ever hummed.

check_hum_note.narration: The note comes up in a pattern: low, high, low, middle. The great eye waits, as if hoping you will answer. Listen, then hum it back the same way.

interaction.cue: Listen to the hums, then hum them back in order.

onSuccess.narration: You hum, and the great eye blinks slowly. The note comes back softer, like a sleepy friend under the covers. It heard you.

onFailure.narration: Your note comes out as a squeak. The great eye crinkles. It might be laughing. The note that comes back sounds friendlier.

onAssisted.narration: The Seal-Keeper hums the first note, soft as a purr, and you follow. The great eye blinks slowly. It heard you.

check_hear_titan.narration: You press your ear to the warm glass. The sounds come in pieces, all part of one question. Share what everyone hears, then put the sounds in order.

interaction.cue: Share what you hear, then choose the sounds in order.
clues: It starts with the low rumble.
The chime comes just before the sigh.

onSuccess.narration: It is a question, the same sounds over and over, like a little kid at bedtime. "Yes," says the Seal-Keeper. "You hear it too."

onFailure.narration: All you hear is a hum that makes your ear itch. "It is asking something," says the Seal-Keeper. "It always asks the same thing."

onAssisted.narration: The Seal-Keeper listens with you. Rumble, chime, sigh, over and over, like a bedtime question. "Yes," it says. "You hear it too."

scene_seal_chamber.narration: Now the whole truth: every gemstone the mountain ever threw out is a piece of the seal. Under it sleeps the titan. The seal is its blanket, and every stone carried off let the cold in. Now it is waking, not angry, only asking: "Is it morning? Should I get up?" A crown stone, bigger than your head, holds the seal together. "Today it asked you," says the Keeper. "Mend the seal, and it sleeps. Turn it, and it goes for good. Leash it, and someone holds its power. Or take the crown stone, and I hold the seal alone."

variants.text: You look at the gaps in the seal, and then at your empty hands. Whatever you answer, you will answer with what you brought, which is {party}.
In your packs, {facets} of the great stones tug toward the gaps, like a dog that has smelled home.
Your packs pull toward the gaps so hard you plant your feet. All {facets} great stones want to go home.

scene_restore_begin.narration: "Not yet," you tell it. "Go back to sleep. We brought your blanket back." The Seal-Keeper sighs with relief. But the titan is rolling over, and the pieces slide like a puzzle that will not hold still.

variants.text: You have only rush gems and your hands. "Hands will do," says the Keeper. "Hold the pieces while I breathe on them."
You take out {facets} of the great stones. Each one tugs toward its own gap.
You take out all {facets} great stones. They tug toward the gaps so hard your packs nearly fly open.

check_restore_fit.prompt: Match every piece to its own gap while the seal slides about

onSuccess.narration: This one here, that one there. You slot the pieces in as fast as the gaps move, and each one clicks home like a key in its own lock.

onFailure.narration: A piece goes in upside down and pops straight back out, right at your nose. The Seal-Keeper catches it with one claw and turns it the right way around. Click.

check_restore_hold.prompt: Lean on the rolling seal and hold every piece still

onSuccess.narration: You lean on the seal with everything you have, and it holds still. The Seal-Keeper breathes on the cracks, warm and slow, and they set like toffee.

onFailure.narration: The seal bucks, and everybody bounces. But you keep your hands on it, and slowly the Keeper's warm breath sets the cracks like toffee.

scene_restore_last_gap.narration: One gap is left, under the crown stone. The titan's eye is nearly shut. "Something to finish it," says the Seal-Keeper. "Anything given on purpose."

scene_restore_last_gap_gems.narration: You turn out every pocket. Little rush gems pour into the gap. They should not be enough. But they fill it to the top, humming, and the seal shines.

scene_restore_last_gap_little_stone.narration: You set Tansy's pink stone in the gap and say her sorry out loud. It fits exactly. The titan's eye crinkles, as if it waited all day for a sorry.

check_lullaby.prompt: Hum the old note slow and soft, like a lullaby, until the eye closes

onSuccess.narration: You hum, slow and soft. The great eye droops, and droops, and the last gap fills with light all by itself, like a window when somebody inside lights a lamp.

onFailure.narration: You yawn halfway through, which is not very helpful. But yawns are catching. The titan yawns too, a warm wind that blows your hair straight back, and the last gap fills with light.

scene_titan_sleeps.narration: The great eye closes, slow as a sunset. A warm sigh tumbles every embermoth head over heels. The seal clicks whole, and the shaking stops. "It said thank you," says the Seal-Keeper. "It never has before."

scene_titan_sleeps_stay.narration: You sit by the glowing seal. The Seal-Keeper curls up beside you like a very large cat. At last the mountain gives a sleepy rumble that clearly means: go home.

scene_destroy_begin.narration: "Sleep for good," you say. The Seal-Keeper is quiet a long time. "The seal turns like a wheel," it says. "Turned all the way, it lets go." It does not say if that is good.

check_turn_wheel.prompt: Put your shoulders to the huge stone wheel and turn it all the way around

onSuccess.narration: It grinds, then rolls, then turns all the way around, smooth as a millstone. The red light under the glass goes soft and gold.

onFailure.narration: It sticks halfway, and your feet slide. Then the Seal-Keeper sets its tail beside your shoulders, and together, slowly, the wheel turns all the way around. The red light goes soft and gold.

check_wheel_latch.prompt: Hunt along the edge of the wheel for the old latch that lets it turn

onSuccess.narration: There! A little stone latch shaped like a sleeping moth. You flip it, and the wheel turns all the way around by itself, smooth as a millstone. The red light under the glass goes soft and gold.

onFailure.narration: You poke every bump on the wheel. The ninth one is the latch, and it pinches your finger. Ow. But the wheel turns, slowly, all the way around, and the red light goes soft and gold.

scene_titan_goes.narration: The great eye opens one last time and looks at you, not angry at all, the way you look at a place you are leaving. It hums the old note, soft as the end of a song. All over the cave, the rush gems go quiet.

scene_titan_goes_hum.narration: You hum along, and for one note the cave is full of song. Then it is only you, in the quiet. The Seal-Keeper hums the very end with you, badly.

scene_titan_goes_listen.narration: You stand still and listen until there is nothing left to hear. The Seal-Keeper stands beside you. A moth lands on your shoulder, so nobody listens alone.

scene_tether.narration: The titan stirs, and its power rises toward your hands like warm bathwater. It needs a leash and a holder. Up the tube come warden whistles, and humming: Hessa's masked choir has climbed after you to sing it a cure. "Whose hand?" asks the Seal-Keeper. "A tether made on the road holds best. Bare hands may slip. If they do, let go."

scene_tether_call_voss.narration: You shout for the wardens. Captain Voss runs down the tube with Pellam and a line of wardens, all carrying ledgers. She salutes the dragon, which nobody has ever done, and holds out her hands.

scene_wardens_come.narration: You shout up the tube, and down come the Skywardens, out of breath and still very neat. "We will build it a cage," says Captain Voss. "Pass the leash to me."

check_pass_leash.prompt: Pass the bucking leash hand to hand across the shaking cave without letting go

onSuccess.narration: Hand to hand, quick as a bucket line, the leash goes across the cave and into Captain Voss's hands. She does not drop it. Wardens never drop things.

onFailure.narration: The leash bucks and drags you halfway across the floor, but you do not let go. Captain Voss grabs your collar, then the leash, and holds on.

scene_cage_closes.narration: The wardens build a cage of oaths around the seal. Every bar is a promise, written down twice. It holds: honest, careful and cold. Under the glass, the titan's eye blinks at the bars, puzzled.

scene_leash_held.narration: The leash settles in your hands like a sleepy dog on a lead. Under the glass, the titan's eye looks up at you, then closes halfway. Waiting. "Well," says the Seal-Keeper. "Now you are the weather."

scene_chord_held.narration: Hessa's choir sings its chord into the seal, and you hold them to every word of the bargain. The titan hums back, and the red light turns gold. "It's listening," Hessa whispers, crying.

check_tether_self.prompt: Hold the leash steady, every hand on it

onSuccess.narration: It pulls, and pulls, every hand on it pulling back. Then, all at once, it stops pulling.

onFailure.narration: It pulls once, hard, and the leash starts to slide through every one of your hands.

check_tether_cult.narration: You call up the tube for Hessa, and she comes at once, as if she had been waiting on the stair all along. Behind her come her friends from the Deep Hollow in their painted bark masks, humming one low note. Hessa looks at the leash, then at the tether in your hands. "We'll sing," she says. "You keep us to the bargain."
check_tether_cult.prompt: Hold the Deep Hollow choir to every word of the bargain

onSuccess.narration: You read the bargain back to them line by line, twice, like a warden clerk. They keep every word.

onFailure.narration: The choir sings one note more than the bargain said. Just one. The seal shivers, and Hessa's face falls before anyone else's.

scene_tether_slipping.narration: The leash bucks like a kite in a storm, and the seal groans. One more pull and something will crack. "Let go, or hold on," says the Seal-Keeper. "Only one is safe."

check_tether_haul.prompt: Dig in your heels and haul the leash back before it cracks the seal

onSuccess.narration: You dig in your heels and haul, and haul, and the leash stops sliding. It has decided you are in charge.

onFailure.narration: You haul with everything you have, and the leash slips through every hand on it.

scene_tether_let_go.narration: You let go. The leash snaps back under the seal like a rubber band, and the mountain says OOF. The seal holds. The leash is gone for good. "Good," says the Seal-Keeper. "Choose again."

scene_chord_slipping.narration: One extra note wobbles, and a hair-thin crack runs across the seal. The singers have their eyes shut behind their masks. Hessa sees it. "Help!" she says. "Find the right note, or stop the song."

check_chord_catch.prompt: Hum the right note back to the choir before the crack runs

onSuccess.narration: You find the note and hum it, loud and wobbly, and the whole choir catches it from you. The crack closes like a zipper.

onFailure.narration: You hum, but the extra note is louder. The crack runs all the way across, and Hessa's face falls before anyone else's.

scene_chord_stopped.narration: You wave your arms until the singers stop. The crack fades. Hessa sits down and cries a little, and a singer pats her head. The cure is gone for good. "Choose again," says the Seal-Keeper, gently.

ending_heroes.narration: You walk out into morning, and every bell in the foothills rings the happy ring. The embermoths come home in one glowing cloud. At the tree line, Tansy's family waves, goat and all. Under the mountain, the titan sleeps, snug under its mended seal. History calls you the Heroes of Red Sky.

variants.text: You gave back only rush gems and your own hands. History underlines that twice.
Under STONES RETURNED, the history books list {facets}, and where each came from.
Your list of STONES RETURNED fills a page: {facets} great stones, all home.

ending_heroes_destroy.narration: You walk out of a quiet mountain. The titan is gone, gently, like the last note of a song, and nobody will ever know what it was. At the tree line, Tansy's family listens to the quiet. History calls you the Heroes of Red Sky. And the Seal-Keeper, with nothing left to keep, flies out of the mountain at last, embermoths riding on its back.

variants.text: History notes that you brought no stones at all. The Keeper tells the sky first.
Your {facets} great stones stop humming. You keep them anyway, wrapped up warm.

ending_quiet_fixers.narration: You slip out a side tunnel and never tell a soul. The tremors stop, the moths come home, the titan sleeps. History calls it a lucky year, and Tansy's family never knows who to thank. But four hundred years from now, a warden clerk will find one line in an odd-colored ledger, and smile, and wonder who. The Quiet Fixers.

variants.text: The ledger line says: came with empty hands, left the same way.
The line is short, the way you meant it: stones put back, {facets}. No names.
Under the line is a number, {facets}. The clerk counts twice and still cannot believe it.
You came for treasure. You go home with the best secret in the realm instead.

Hessa never finds out who did it. She guesses, and sends extra soup all winter.
Next spring, Hessa finds your coins in her soup-tent tin. Nobody tells her who.
Some nights, far up the mountain, a tiny bell rings the happy ring all by itself.

ending_collectors.narration: You carry the Keystone down the mountain, warm and humming. Whatever you were collecting, it is complete. Behind you, the Seal-Keeper lies across the seal to hold it, and under it the titan lies awake. At the tree line, Tansy stares with round eyes. History calls you The Collectors. A grandmother adds your names to a very old list.

variants.text: You climbed with empty hands. The Keystone is the first stone you ever kept.
Your collection is small and heavy at the top: {facets} great stones, one bigger than your head.
With the Keystone, your collection is {facets} great stones. Every crab on the ash field watches you pass.
You came for treasure, and you got the biggest one there is.
You came to find out what happened. The answer is in your arms, still humming.

You came to keep folk safe. The Seal-Keeper does that now. You visit every spring, with snacks.

Hessa comes to see the Keystone once. She says nothing, and leaves you soup anyway.
Hessa's masked singers ask to sing to the Keystone once a year. It hums back.
The wardens post a guard outside your door. She is excellent at checkers.
The grandmothers make up a ring for you. Nobody knows if it means thank you or watch out.
You keep the Keystone close. It hums softly, like a cat that has picked its people.

ending_wardens_regret.narration: You walk out behind the wardens. The realm is safe, the way a locked room is safe. Under the mountain, the titan waits in its cage. At the tree line, Tansy asks if the thing in the cage minds. Nobody can tell her. Years later, Captain Voss writes: I wonder if it was lonely. History calls it The Wardens' Regret. But the embermoths still visit the titan every evening.

variants.text: Beside your names, the ledger says STONES SURRENDERED: none. Captain Voss calls it the most honest line in the book.
Beside your names, STONES SURRENDERED says {facets}, written neatly and checked twice.
STONES SURRENDERED runs off the page: {facets} great stones, each logged twice.
You came for treasure. The wardens give you a very neat receipt instead.

Hessa does not argue about the cage. She sends the titan a song every evening.
Hessa asks that your soup-tent coins buy something kinder than a cage. You keep her letter.
You told the wardens first. Pellam keeps a chair for you at the truth-table, with a cushion.
The grandmothers ring a slow ring each evening for whatever is in the cage.
You kept it close all the way, then gave it away. The wardens still wonder about you.

ending_cure.narration: You walk out with the Deep Hollow choir still singing, and under the seal the titan hums along. Hessa's choir swears the world is mending. Maybe it is: the sky is a little less red, and Hessa cries into a pot of soup. Tansy hums the chord all the way home. History calls it The Cure, with a question mark nobody can rub out.

variants.text: The choir sings a short song about climbers who carried nothing. Hessa says short ones are truest.
Your great stones sing in the chord too, {facets} small notes of their own.
The choir rings the seal with your {facets} great stones, and the chord rattles windows for miles.
You came for treasure. Hessa pays you in soup forever, which is honestly fair.
You came to find out what happened. Hessa says you will have to wait and see.
You came to be famous. The choir sings your names in a chord, the loudest way there is.
You came to keep folk safe. Whether this does, nobody knows yet, so you keep watching.
You came for a fresh start. Hessa says the whole world is having one. She may be right.
You came to prove you could. You held a whole choir to its word.
You said no to Hessa's cure once, then handed it to her anyway. She laughs about that for years.
Your soup-tent coins helped pay for the chord. Hessa shows you the receipt, very proudly.
The wardens add a question mark, and send a warden to sing with the choir.
The grandmothers ring for the choir, the choir sings back, and by spring nobody can tell which is which.
You kept it close until the end, then trusted Hessa. She keeps that trust like her best ladle.

ending_new_weather.narration: You walk out holding the leash, and the titan lies half awake, in your keeping. The realm has something new: you. Farmers watch your camp to know if it will rain. Tansy's family plants beans by your weather, and the beans have never been happier. History calls you The New Weather. The Seal-Keeper sometimes visits for tea.

variants.text: You climbed the mountain with empty packs. Somehow, that is why the farmers trust you.
You keep {facets} of the great stones in a jar. When it hums, farmers bring in the washing.
You keep all {facets} great stones on your windowsill. When they hum together, thunder rolls.
You came for treasure. Farmers bring you pies to ask about rain. That is better, mostly.

You came to prove you could. You hold the power under a mountain. Nobody asks for proof now.

Hessa thanks you for your soup-tent coins, and asks for rain on Tuesdays.
The wardens send a clerk to log your weather twice a day. Pellam gets the job.
The grandmothers make a ring for every weather. The rain ring is the little ones' favorite.
You kept it close the whole way, and you keep it close still, like a sleeping bird.

ending_turned_back.narration: The Seal-Keeper never hurts children who come up the wrong way. It sets you down in the foothills with everybody else, then goes back to hold the seal alone. You watch the summit glow all night. At dawn, an embermoth lands on your hand and stays. It only does that for someone it expects to see again.

All {facets} great stones hum toward the summit so loudly that the whole foothills keeps watch with you.

The grandmothers ring the ordinary bell all night, so the Keeper is not holding alone.
Nobody knew you went up. But you know, and the moth knows. That is enough to start again.

ending_last_ring.narration: The ring nobody ever used rings across the realm. Something enormous stretches under the mountain, and nobody is at the seal to answer. The realm does not end. It rearranges: rivers wander, roads bend, the red sky turns ordinary. History calls you the almost-heroes. But in the foothills, a dragonling child is already learning the bell code backwards, looking for a ring to put it all back to sleep.

variants.text: You carried no stones at all. The dragonling child says that makes it braver.
In your packs, {facets} of the great stones ring faintly with the last bell.
All {facets} great stones ring with the last bell, loud as a second bell.
You came for treasure. Now it is scattered across a brand-new map.
You came to find out what happened. Now there is a whole new realm to learn.
You came to be famous. They call you the almost-heroes. You plan to drop the almost.
You came to keep folk safe. Folk are scattered, not gone, and you go to find them.
You came for a fresh start. The whole realm got one, and somebody has to help.

Hessa's soup tents are the first thing open in the new realm. She just ladles.
Your soup-tent coins buy blankets for everyone whose roof wandered off.
The wardens start a new log: WHERE EVERYTHING WENT. You help fill it in.
The grandmothers ring every bell they have left, and one by one, far away, bells answer.
Nobody knew you went up. But you know where the seal is now, and you are already planning how to fix it.

ending_broken_tether.narration: The leash snaps, and the seal cracks. The titan rolls over, half awake, and the mountain throws gemstones across the sky. The Seal-Keeper throws itself across the crack and holds it. Everybody who reached for that leash grieves. But the seal is cracked, not broken, and the Keeper is still holding. Holding is something somebody can help with, someday.

variants.text: You had only your hands, and you held on anyway. That counts, the Keeper says. A lot.

You came for treasure. Now the sky is full of it, and you help people pick it up.
You came to find out what happened. Now you know the titan best, and that will help.
You came to be famous. The Keeper calls your names when it needs a hand. Good famous.

You came for a fresh start. The realm has a crack now, and fresh starts mend cracks.
You came to prove you could. Not this time. You are already working out how.

You kept it close, and now it is yours to help mend. You go back in spring.

check_tether_self_bare.prompt: Hold the leash with nothing but your own hands

onSuccess.narration: No tether this time, only hands, so you become the tether. It pulls, and pulls, and then it stops. The Seal-Keeper blinks, which it has not done in a very long time.

onFailure.narration: Bare hands are not enough. It pulls once, hard, and starts to slide through every hand on it.

check_tether_cult_bare.narration: You call up the tube for Hessa, and she comes at once, as if she had been waiting on the stair all along. Behind her come her friends from the Deep Hollow in their painted bark masks, humming one low note. Hessa looks at the leash, then at your empty hands. "We'll sing," she says. "Tell us the bargain, and we'll keep it."
check_tether_cult_bare.prompt: Hold Hessa's singers to a bargain you made up just now

onSuccess.narration: You make the bargain up as you go, and you make it very carefully. Hessa reads it twice and nods. They keep every word.

onFailure.narration: Nobody wrote the bargain down, so Hessa's singers sing it the way they remember it, one note more than you meant. The seal shivers, and Hessa's face falls before anyone else's.

scene_keystone.narration: The crown stone is bigger than your head and warm as bread. Under it, the titan's eye opens wide. "Collectors may lift it," says the Seal-Keeper. "Anyone else must pry, and gets one try."

variants.text: Your hands are all you brought. They look very small next to it.
In your packs, {facets} great stones hum louder and louder, as if they know what is about to join them.

check_keystone.prompt: Pry the crown stone out of a seal that does not want to let it go

onSuccess.narration: It comes loose with a sound like a cork from the biggest bottle in the world. You did not come up here for this. You are holding it anyway.

onFailure.narration: The crown stone does not budge. It is hot as an oven door, and your hands sting. Then the Seal-Keeper puts one claw on it, very gently, and the decision is no longer yours.

scene_keystone_refused.narration: The Seal-Keeper lifts your hands off the crown stone one finger at a time, like unsticking a starfish. "Not that one," it says. "Not today, and not by you."

scene_keystone_lifted.narration: The Keystone comes free in your arms, warm as a sleeping cat. The seal shudders, and the great eye flies open. The Seal-Keeper lies down across the seal. "Go," it says. "I will always hold the door."

interaction_bundles.narration: Down the slope, the faun family is stuck: their goat has parked the cart across a washed-out step. You help pass the bundles over, hand to hand. Tansy's mother hands you a warm honeycake. "For being kind to my small one."

scene_warden_post_tin.narration: Clink. The tin pops open. Inside is a brave whistle on a string, tagged FOR A LOUD MOMENT. You sign the log too, in small letters.

interaction_chimney.narration: Above the post, the stair turns into a steep chimney of warm rock. A rope hangs down it. A sign says: ONE CLIMBER AT A TIME. EVERYBODY ELSE HOLDS THE ROPE.

interaction.cue: Friends hold the rope steady while someone climbs.

onSuccess.narration: Hand over hand, up you go. You pop out at the top with your hair full of cloud.

onFailure.narration: The rope swings, and you slide to a ledge on your bottom. You take the long way, and pop out with your hair full of cloud.

onAssisted.narration: Everybody holds the rope, and you climb one slow hand at a time. You pop out with your hair full of cloud.

scene_crab_guards.narration: At the far side, the two biggest crabs block the only way up, claws raised. They think you came to dig. Crabs cannot be argued with. They can be bumped, gently.

encounter_crabs.narration: The guard crabs click, clack and puff out their glassy backs. Bump them off the path before they bump you.

scene_crabs_bumped.narration: The crabs tip over like teacups and right themselves, very offended. The oldest scuttles aside, uncovering three old coins and a lucky-looking stone. It pushes them to you.

scene_crabs_herded.narration: The crabs bump you until you sit down in the ash, giggling. Then they herd you onto the path like sheepdogs. The oldest pats your boot.

interaction_climb_warmup.narration: Everyone is running down Mount Red Sky. Tonight you climb the mountain everyone else is running from, find the seal deep inside, and give your answer. First, rub your cold hands.

interaction_verdict_council.narration: "Who did you tell, and what do you want?" The Seal-Keeper lowers its head to listen. Give every hero a turn: something you carried, someone who helped, or what should happen now.

interaction_restore_fit.narration: One of your stones hums beside its own gap. Listen for the match, set the stone in place, then hold it steady while the Keeper warms the seal.

interaction.cue: Arrange the steps: listen, fit, then hold steady.

options.label: Fit the stone in its own gap
Keep it steady as the seal warms

clues: The right gap answers the stone before anyone touches it.
A stone must be placed before it can be held still.
The Keeper warms the seal only after the pieces are in place.

onSuccess.narration: Each piece finds a home, then settles under your hands. Only the last gap remains.

onFailure.narration: A stone slips and bumps your fingers. The Keeper helps you fit it. Only the last gap remains.

onAssisted.narration: The Keeper hums back each note so you can find its gap. Together you finish all but the last one.

interaction_wheel_latch.narration: The stone wheel turns a little, then sticks. Under its rim, a small moth-shaped latch is moving. Wait for the wheel to settle, then catch the latch gently.

interaction.cue: Stop at the calm place to release the latch.

onSuccess.narration: Click. The latch opens, and the wheel turns all the way. The old note goes soft.

onFailure.narration: The latch pinches your fingers, but the Keeper steadies the wheel. Together you turn it all the way.

onAssisted.narration: The Keeper braces the rim as you feel for the latch. It opens, and the wheel turns gently.

interaction_leash_transfer.narration: The wardens make a line, the one your warning made possible. Captain Voss waits at the end. Catch the bucking leash and pass it along to her.

interaction.cue: Catch the leash and pass it along the prepared line.

onSuccess.narration: Hand to hand, the leash reaches Captain Voss. She braces it while the wardens make their promises.

onFailure.narration: The line wobbles, but the wardens steady the leash before it reaches Captain Voss.

onAssisted.narration: Pellam steps into the gap, and together you pass the leash safely to Captain Voss.

interaction_restore_brace.narration: The Keeper sets a claw on the cracked seal. Hold the loose pieces while its warm breath joins them. A moth helps by sitting on a crack. It has misunderstood the job.

interaction.cue: Brace the loose pieces while the Keeper warms the cracks.

onSuccess.narration: Your hands and the Keeper's claw hold the pieces still. The cracks join. One last gap remains.

onFailure.narration: A piece slips. The Keeper steadies it with another claw. Together you join the cracks.

onAssisted.narration: The Keeper braces beside you. Together you hold the pieces until the cracks join.

interaction_verdict_council_response_car.narration: The dragon asks what changed because you carried it. Then it moves aside. "You came a long way to give your own answers," it says.

interaction_verdict_council_response_hel.narration: An embermoth settles closer to listen. Then it moves aside. "You came a long way to give your own answers," it says.

interaction_verdict_council_response_cho.narration: The Seal-Keeper waits until your answer is complete. Then it moves aside. "You came a long way to give your own answers," it says.

voiceGuide.tone: the campaign's finale: awe, warmth, and consequence; the dragon is ancient, dry and fair; losses are grief and consequence, never gore, and always end on a spark
forbidden: explaining what the Hollow Gate is

npcVoices.seal_keeper: the Seal-Keeper, the legend dragon under Mount Red Sky; ancient, unhurried, dry as ash, asks questions it already knows the answers to, grades generously when surprised and is very rarely surprised
npcVoices.bones: the restless remains; do not speak, but nod, sigh and settle
npcVoices.captain: Captain Orla Voss of the Skywardens, only in epilogues; rigid, honest, quietly sorry
npcVoices.hessa: Hessa Wren of the Deep Hollow Cult, only in epilogues; warm, certain, cries easily
npcVoices.tansy: Tansy, a small faun girl running downhill with her family; worried, brave, and very honest about the humming stone in her pocket
npcVoices.titan: the titan under the seal; never described or explained, only witnessed: a great sleepy eye, a warm breath, and the old note the stones hum, which the Seal-Keeper puts into words; curious, slow and never angry

interaction_climb_warmup.narration: At Mount Red Sky, everyone else is running downhill. You must climb, find the seal and answer what is waking below. Cold fingers first: wake your hands and boots before the rocks put them to work.

interaction.cue: Warm up before the mountain climb.

options.label: Stamp your boots
options.reaction: Loose grit dances around your feet.

options.label: Stretch up high
options.reaction: The summit still looks very far away.

options.label: Shake out your hands
options.reaction: Your fingers feel ready for the rocks.

interaction_bundles.narration: Down the slope, the faun family has stopped again. Their goat has parked the cart across a washed-out step, and it will not budge. Tansy's father waves both arms at you. "Help us pass the bundles over the gap, hand to hand!" he calls. "Quick, before the goat has opinions!"

interaction.cue: Catch the bundle, then pass it along.

onSuccess.narration: Bundle after bundle goes over the gap, and not one lands in the mud. The goat watches the whole thing, chewing. Tansy's mother presses a warm honeycake into your hands. "For the climb," she says, "and for being nice to my small one."

onFailure.narration: One bundle bursts open, and a whole pillow's worth of feathers floats down the mountain like snow. The goat sneezes. The family laughs, and the cart rolls on.

onAssisted.narration: Together you and Tansy's father pass the bundles in a slow, steady row, and not one lands in the mud. Tansy's mother presses a warm honeycake into your hands. "For the climb," she says.

interaction_verdict_council.narration: The Keeper asks whom you told and what you want. Make room for every hero: name something carried, remember a helper, or say what should happen now. The dragon lowers its head to listen.

interaction.cue: Each hero shares one thing they carried, learned, or chose.

options.label: Name something I carried
options.reaction: The dragon asks what changed because you carried it.

options.label: Remember someone who helped
options.reaction: An embermoth settles closer to listen.

options.label: Say what I want for the realm
options.reaction: The Seal-Keeper waits until your answer is complete.

onSuccess.narration: The dragon heard everyone. It moves aside. "You came a long way to give your own answers," it says.

onFailure.narration: The Keeper helps find the words and makes room for the party at the seal.

onAssisted.narration: The Keeper asks a question at a time. Together you finish your answer, and it lets you pass.
